contributions.statement: In an agent acceptance-test repair loop, re-run the full acceptance suite every round and keep the best checkpoint rather than the last one: broad whole-project repairs regressed previously passing features (MiniMax peaked at round 3 and then regressed in 14 of 20 apps).
contributions.evidence: §5.3.2 Table 8: per-round loop-internal tester accuracy and regression counts across Whole-Project repair attempts (K=5). 20 small greenfield web apps, single run per cell.

contributions.statement: Prefer one whole-project test-and-repair pass per round over per-feature incremental or fully agent-driven TDD when cost matters: it delivered 65% of the agentic gain at ~2.7x fewer additional tokens, because 96% of tokens are re-read context; switch to bounded per-feature loops when the feedback model is weak.
contributions.evidence: §5.4 Table 9 (4.97-10.33 pp per million extra tokens, best in 4 of 5 configurations) and §5.3.1. Confound: the loop sees acceptance tests converted from the same tests the oracle scores.

contributions.statement: A TDD loop helps only if the failure-interpreting verifier is reliable: with Qwen3.5 judging its own tests, 56% of executions were labelled failures, 49% of features were abandoned and accuracy fell below no-TDD.
contributions.evidence: §5.2.2 Tables 6-7. Audit: the 'stronger tester' swapped in is also the final oracle model, and two of three recovered gains are p=.056/.092.
relative_to: P16 execution-based verifier loops (2608.16742 self-contradiction failure mode)

reason: The headline +15-24 pp is inflated because the loop sees the oracle's tests. The checkpoint and loop-granularity findings come from per-round traces and are actionable for a spec-to-acceptance-test rollout.
